questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is NOT part of the fore-stomach compartments of a ruminant:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Abomasum (2 marks)
The fore-stomach compartments of a ruminant are the rumen, reticulum and omasum. The abomasum is the 'true' (glandular) stomach and is not part of the fore-stomach.

subQuestions.questionText: An example of a protein-rich concentrate:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Carcass meal (2 marks)
Carcass meal (meat meal) is an animal by-product with a very high protein content. Maize meal, oat meal and wheat meal are energy-rich (carbohydrate) concentrates.

subQuestions.questionText: Tubular indentations of the epithelium between the villi that secrete succus entericus:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Glands of Lieberkühn (2 marks)
The crypts (glands) of Lieberkühn are tubular glands between the villi of the small intestine that secrete intestinal juice (succus entericus).

subQuestions.questionText:
A nutritive ratio of 1 : 4 implies that:
(i) The feed has high protein content
(ii) The feed is suitable for growth and reproduction
(iii) For every one part of carbohydrates, there are four parts of protein
(iv) For every one part of protein, there are four parts of non-nitrogenous compounds
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
A nutritive ratio of 1 : 4 is narrow, so the feed is high in protein and suitable for growth and reproduction, and for every 1 part protein there are 4 parts non-nitrogenous compounds (carbohydrates + fat). Statement (iii) reverses the ratio and is wrong.

subQuestions.questionText: A farmer producing crops or livestock to generate profit using highly advanced technologies:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Commercial farmer (2 marks)
A commercial farmer produces on a large scale, using advanced technology, mainly to generate profit. Subsistence and communal farmers produce mainly for their own use.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following are the requirements for an ideal poultry housing facility:
(i) Lengthwise orientation should be in a north-south direction.
(ii) The roof must be high and insulated.
(iii) Side walls should keep running water away from the house.
(iv) Side walls should not allow air movement through the house.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - (i), (ii) and (iii) (2 marks)
A poultry house should run north-south (to limit direct sun into the house), have a high, insulated roof, and be sited so that run-off water is led away. Statement (iv) is wrong because the house must allow air movement (ventilation).

subQuestions.questionText: The microscopic organisms that live outside the body of the host, which cause the crusted skin leading to a loss of wool:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Mites (2 marks)
Mites are microscopic external parasites that burrow into the skin and cause sheep scab, with crusted skin and loss of wool. Ticks and lice are visible to the naked eye.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is NOT a sign of poor health in farm animals:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Bright eyes with pink membranes (2 marks)
Bright eyes with pink mucous membranes indicate a healthy animal. A rough dull coat, abnormal faeces/urine and raised temperature and pulse are signs of poor health.

options.A: Rough and dull coat with hair loss
options.B: Too soft faeces and discoloured urine
options.D: High body temperature and increased pulse rate

subQuestions.questionText: A sign of a cow approaching parturition:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - Urinates and defecates often (2 marks)
Frequent urination and defecation, restlessness, swelling of the udder and vulva and a sunken pelvis are signs of approaching parturition. The other options are signs of oestrus.

options.C: Follows the bulls and other cows

subQuestions.questionText: A factor that results in infertility in cows:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - Metritis (2 marks)
Metritis (inflammation/infection of the uterus) damages the reproductive tract and causes infertility in cows. Cryptorchidism and castration relate to males; super ovulation increases offspring numbers.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A. Write A only, B only, both A and B or none.
COLUMN A: A: Bile; B: Liver
COLUMN B: Breaks down fats into fine droplets
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A only (2 marks)
Bile emulsifies fats, breaking large fat globules into fine droplets. The liver produces bile but does not itself break down the fats.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Pharynx; B: Tongue
COLUMN B: An organ that helps farm animals to distinguish between different feeds
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B only (2 marks)
The tongue carries the taste buds and, with the sense of taste, helps the animal distinguish between feeds. The pharynx is a passage shared by the digestive and respiratory tracts.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Heterothermic; B: Homeothermic
COLUMN B: The ability of farm animals to maintain a constant body temperature
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B only (2 marks)
Homeothermic (warm-blooded) animals maintain a constant body temperature. Heterothermic animals allow their body temperature to vary with the environment.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Thorn apple; B: Poison bulb
COLUMN B: Poisonous plants that should be prevented by avoiding storing feeds under wet conditions
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
Poisoning that is prevented by not storing feed under wet conditions is mould/fungal (mycotoxin) poisoning. Thorn apple and poison bulb are toxic growing plants, not storage moulds.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether each of the descriptions in COLUMN B applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN A.
COLUMN A: A: Prostaglandin; B: Progesterone
COLUMN B: Hormones used in synchronising oestrus in cows
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
Both prostaglandin (to regress the corpus luteum) and progesterone / progestagens (to hold cows out of heat and then release them together) are used in oestrus synchronisation programmes.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The enzyme that breaks down starch molecules, especially in pigs.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Amylase / ptyalin (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The small area where sheep are kept under intensive conditions and fed for maximum production.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Feedlot (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
A reproductive technique where semen is collected from a superior bull and deposited into the reproductive tract of a cow in oestrus.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Artificial insemination / AI (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
Cows that need to mate three or more times before conceiving.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Repeat breeders (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description. Write only the word/term.
The inability of a bull to service cows that are in oestrus even though it has interest.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Impotence (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Digestible energy refers to the energy left after deducting energy loss through heat from metabolic energy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Net energy / NE (1 mark)
Net energy is the energy left after the heat increment (energy lost as heat) is deducted from metabolic energy.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The introduction of natural enemies to control parasite infestation is a chemical method.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Biological (1 mark)
Using natural enemies (predators/parasites of the pest) is a biological control method.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
The centriole releases an enzyme that assists the sperm cell to penetrate the ovum.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Acrosome (1 mark)
The acrosome (cap over the sperm head) releases enzymes that digest the wall of the ovum so that the sperm can penetrate.

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Di-oestrus happens when sexually mature female animals show no signs of standing heat.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Anoestrus (1 mark)
Anoestrus is a period during which a sexually mature female shows no signs of oestrus (standing heat).

subQuestions.questionText:
Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) in the following statement to make it TRUE. Write only the answer.
Gestation period refers to the period in cows between two lactations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Dry period / rest period (1 mark)
The dry (rest) period is the time between the end of one lactation and the start of the next. Gestation is the period of pregnancy.

subQuestions.questionText:
The picture in the question paper shows the alimentary canal of a sheep drawn inside the outline of the animal. Label A points to the mouth; label G points to the oesophagus; labels B, C and D point to the compartments at the top of the compound stomach; labels F and E point to compartments lower down; the small and large intestines are also shown.
Identify in the picture above only the LETTER of the PART where EACH of the following occurs:
(a) Microbial fermentation
(b) Mechanical digestion
(c) Chemical digestion
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Microbial fermentation - B / C (1 mark) – the rumen / reticulum
(b) Mechanical digestion - A / F (1 mark) – the mouth (chewing) / omasum (grinding)
(c) Chemical digestion - E / D (1 mark) – the abomasum (true stomach)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE function of the small intestine.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Absorption of the digested food / nutrients
• Secretion of digestive juices to break down larger molecules
• Assists in mixing food with the digestive juices
• Undigested / unabsorbed contents pass through to the large intestine

subQuestions.questionText: Compare the structure of the oesophagus in sheep with that of fowl.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE comparison (2 marks):
• In sheep the oesophagus has no enlargement / crop ✓, but in fowls the oesophagus has an enlargement / crop ✓
• In sheep the oesophagus is wide / long ✓, in fowls the oesophagus is narrow / short ✓

subQuestions.questionText:
The biological value of protein is determined by the amino acid composition and some other factors. Animals need amino acids that their bodies cannot produce, but in ruminant animals the protein quality of feeds is of less importance.
Give a collective name for the amino acids that cannot be produced in animal bodies.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Essential amino acids (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the protein quality of feeds in ruminant animals is of less importance.
subQuestions.memoText: The micro-organisms in the rumen are able to utilise (any) amino acids ✓ to synthesise microbial protein that has a higher biological value ✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
An ox was fed 24 kg dry matter and excreted 7 kg manure with 81% dry material.
Calculate the digestibility coefficient of the feed. Show ALL calculations, including the formula.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – Dry mass of manure = 81/100 × 7 kg = 5,67 kg ✓ (1 mark)
Step 2 – Formula: DC = [(Dry matter intake − Dry mass of manure) ÷ Dry matter intake] × 100 ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – Substitution: = [(24 kg − 5,67 kg) ÷ 24 kg] × 100 ✓ (1 mark)
Step 4 – Answer: = 76,38% ✓✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
The schematic representation in the question paper shows the components of a feed: Feed components split into Dry material and Water; Dry material splits into Organic components and A; Organic components split into B, Lipids, Vitamins and C; C leads to Maltose.
Provide the labels for feed components A and C respectively.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Inorganic components (minerals) (1 mark)
C - Carbohydrates (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO functions of water.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• An important solvent
• Helps during mechanical digestion / moistens food
• Prevents constipation
• Transportation of nutrients
• Eliminates waste products
• Part of biochemical reactions / homeostasis
• Acts as a lubricant
• Regulates body temperature / cooling system
• Supplies turgor pressure in cells / provides shape and firmness to cells
• A major component of cells / blood / body tissue
• Protects sensitive tissues / acts as a shock-absorbing fluid
• For efficient milk production

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the letter that represents the component suitable for feeding young animals for growth.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B (1 mark)
B represents protein, which is needed for growth (building of new tissue) in young animals.

subQuestions.questionText:
A farmer mixed soya bean oilcake meal and oatmeal to obtain a ration with the desired protein content, using the Pearson square shown in the question paper: FEED A (9% DP) gives 29 parts; FEED B (44% DP) gives 6 parts; the desired value in the centre is 15%.
Refer to the Pearson square above to indicate the parts of this ration that represent EACH of the following:
(a) Soya bean oilcake meal
(b) Oatmeal
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Soya bean oilcake meal (44% DP) - 6 parts (1 mark)
(b) Oatmeal (9% DP) - 29 parts (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of oatmeal in the given mixture. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Step 1 – Total parts = 29 + 6 = 35 parts ✓ (1 mark)
Step 2 – Percentage oatmeal = (29 ÷ 35) × 100 ✓ (1 mark)
Step 3 – Answer = 82,86% ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows a fodder flow programme on the provision and feed requirements for beef cattle over a period of one year. The ANIMAL FEED REQUIRED (TON) column is: January 50; February 50; March 50; April 50; May 55; June 60; July 65; August 65; September 60; October 50; November 55; December 50.
Calculate the quantity of feed required (in kg) during the first six months of the year. Show ALL calculations.
Give TWO reasons why fodder flow planning is important.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Safe / efficient use of resources
• To meet the animals' feed requirements / feeding standards throughout the year
• Effective management of the fodder flow programme
• To ensure a positive margin over feed costs

subQuestions.questionText:
Use the data in the table above to draw a line graph on quantities of feed required by beef cattle and the production of lucerne from August to December. The relevant values are:
Feed required (ton): August 65; September 60; October 50; November 55; December 50
Lucerne available (ton): August 45; September 55; October 45; November 30; December 25
subQuestions.memoText:
A line graph with two lines (Feed required and Lucerne production) against month, from August to December.

MARKING CRITERIA (1 mark each):
• Correct heading (e.g. 'Feed requirements of beef cattle and lucerne production from August to December')
• X-axis: correct calibrations and labelled (Month of the year)
• Y-axis: correct calibrations and labelled (Quantities)
• Correct unit (tons)
• Line graph (two lines with a key)
• Accuracy (at least 80% of points correctly plotted)

Points to plot:
• Feed required: (Aug, 65), (Sep, 60), (Oct, 50), (Nov, 55), (Dec, 50)
• Lucerne production: (Aug, 45), (Sep, 55), (Oct, 45), (Nov, 30), (Dec, 25)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures in the question paper refer to a production system in pigs. Picture A shows a sow confined in a metal farrowing crate with her piglets in a slatted-floor pen indoors. Picture B shows a sow and her piglets grazing outdoors on open pasture.
Indicate:
(a) The production system used by the pig farmer represented by picture A above
(b) An example of the pig production system represented in picture B above
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Intensive production system (1 mark)
(b) Free range system (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the animal handling facility in picture A.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Farrowing pen / farrowing crate (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason for housing pigs in the facility in picture A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (1 mark):
• Separates the sow and piglets / prevents cannibalism
• Prevents the sow from rolling over / lying down on the piglets
• Easy management / handling of the animals

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce TWO factors from picture A that contribute to increased production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Environment / housing / sheltering
• Nutrition / feeding
• Management
• Breeding / reproduction

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose an explanation from the list below that matches the animal behaviour. Write only the letter (A–E).
A: See shadow on their path or vision area
B: Normal maternal behaviour
C: Normal animal behaviour
D: Animals establish their dominance in the flock
E: Normal reproductive behaviour
Behaviour: Female animals in the herd mount other females and allow other animals to mount them.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: E (normal reproductive behaviour – it indicates oestrus/standing heat) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose an explanation from the list (A: See shadow on their path or vision area; B: Normal maternal behaviour; C: Normal animal behaviour; D: Animals establish their dominance in the flock; E: Normal reproductive behaviour) that matches the following behaviour. Write only the letter.
Behaviour: A flock of farm animals looks healthy and graze calmly on natural pasture.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: C (normal animal behaviour) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose an explanation from the list (A: See shadow on their path or vision area; B: Normal maternal behaviour; C: Normal animal behaviour; D: Animals establish their dominance in the flock; E: Normal reproductive behaviour) that matches the following behaviour. Write only the letter.
Behaviour: Animals head-butting each other.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: D (animals establish their dominance / social order in the flock) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose an explanation from the list (A: See shadow on their path or vision area; B: Normal maternal behaviour; C: Normal animal behaviour; D: Animals establish their dominance in the flock; E: Normal reproductive behaviour) that matches the following behaviour. Write only the letter.
Behaviour: Animals do not want to enter a gate leading to a passage area.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: A (they see a shadow on their path / in their vision area) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose an explanation from the list (A: See shadow on their path or vision area; B: Normal maternal behaviour; C: Normal animal behaviour; D: Animals establish their dominance in the flock; E: Normal reproductive behaviour) that matches the following behaviour. Write only the letter.
Behaviour: Animals become aggressive after giving birth.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: B (normal maternal behaviour – the dam protects her newborn) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The picture in the question paper shows facilities used for handling farm animals: a strongly built narrow passage that holds cattle single file (labelled A) with a hinged device at the front end that clamps around an animal's neck (labelled B).
Identify facilities A and B above.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Crush / chute (1 mark)
B - Head gate / neck clamp (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the purpose of using facility B (the head gate / neck clamp).
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Restraining the farm animal (holding the head still) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for handling farm animals using the facilities above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Management practices (docking / castration / AI / identification / dehorning / branding)
• For diagnosis purposes
• Application of medication / treatment of parasites
• Transportation
• Generation of data
• Determining the age of the animal
• For pregnancy testing

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO basic requirements for transporting farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Do not transport animals when the roads are busy
• Transport animals of different ages / sizes / sexes / species separately
• Pregnant animals (near term) should not be transported
• Floors should not be slippery
• No sharp edges / angles on the truck
• Facilities (rails) should be high and strong
• Familiarise animals with the loading area
• Do not feed animals less than 12 hours before loading
• Display a red flag when transporting animals by road
• Animals should not be rushed
• Do not load animals too long before departure
• Proper ventilation
• Relevant legal documentation

subQuestions.questionText:
A mosquito-borne viral disease that affects sheep, cattle and goats causes abortion, blood-stained nasal discharge and diarrhoea which may lead to the death of farm animals. People can get infected if they handle blood, tissues or other body fluids of animals that are infected with this disease. Farmers should alert authorities if they suspect that animals are infected with the disease on their farms.
Name the disease described in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Rift Valley Fever (RVF) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify an example of EACH of the following in the scenario above:
(a) Vector
(b) Pathogen
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Vector - Mosquito (1 mark)
(b) Pathogen - Virus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The disease in the scenario above is deemed notifiable. Justify this statement.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: The disease is highly transmittable / infectious / contagious (and can spread rapidly and infect people), so it must be reported to the authorities (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a term for the description which indicates that the disease can infect people if they handle infected blood, tissues and other body fluids.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Zoonotic (zoonosis) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO economic implications of animal diseases to a farmer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Banning of exports and imports / decrease in trade
• High treatment / vaccination costs to control and prevent the disease
• Decreased production
• Loss of livestock / death
• Loss of income / profit

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper shows the life cycle of a parasite (a tick): adults attach to the host (a cow); adult females drop off the host to lay eggs; eggs hatch into six-legged larvae; the larva becomes a nymph on a first host (a rabbit is shown); the nymph moults into an adult that then attaches to the host again.
Classify the parasite above according to the life cycle.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Two-host (parasite) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 3.6.1 by referring to the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: It needs two hosts (a first host for the larva/nymph and another host for the adult) to complete its life cycle (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify THREE stages in the life cycle of the parasite above.
subQuestions.memoText: Any THREE (1 mark each): Adult; Eggs; Larvae; Nymph

subQuestions.questionText:
Below is a list of internal parasites that affect farm animals: tapeworm; liver fluke; roundworm.
Choose the parasite above that matches EACH of the following descriptions:
(a) Causes nodules in the liver
(b) Does not need an intermediate host
(c) Heavy infestation causes a potbelly and the appearance of proglottids in faeces
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Liver fluke (1 mark)
(b) Roundworm (1 mark)
(c) Tapeworm (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO basic principles of good health that a farmer can apply to control internal parasites.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Good sanitation / hygiene
• Practise rotational grazing to control parasites at their breeding areas
• Proper handling / removal of manure
• Isolation of sick animals from healthy ones
• Vaccination
• Veld burning
• Proper feeding (good nutrition to build resistance)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagrams in the question paper show male and female reproductive organs. DIAGRAM 1 (male) has parts A (a gland near the base of the penis), B, C and D (an oval organ inside the scrotum). DIAGRAM 2 (female) has parts E, F, G, H and I, with the bladder also marked.
Label B, C and G in the diagrams above.
subQuestions.memoText:
B - Vas deferens / sperm duct (1 mark)
C - Epididymis (1 mark)
G - Cervix (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the LETTER (A–I) of the part in DIAGRAM 1 and DIAGRAM 2 where EACH of the following occurs:
(a) Site where spermatogenesis occurs
(b) Serves the function of implantation
(c) Site where fertilisation occurs
(d) Secretes a sticky liquid that provides energy to the sperm cells
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Spermatogenesis - D (testis) (1 mark)
(b) Implantation - E (uterus / uterine horn) (1 mark)
(c) Fertilisation - I (oviduct / fallopian tube) (1 mark)
(d) Sticky liquid providing energy to sperm - A (seminal vesicle) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The picture in the question paper shows a cow and a bull during a reproductive process, with the bull raised up on its hind legs and its forelegs resting over the back of the cow.
Identify the reproductive process represented in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Mating / copulation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the actual stage of the process in QUESTION 4.2.1 represented in the picture.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Mounting (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO sexual behavioural signs that are displayed by bulls before the process in QUESTION 4.2.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Follows / is excited about the cow on oestrus closely
• Smelling / licking the external genitalia and urine of the cow
• Extends the head and curls the upper lip (Flehmen response)
• Pawing on the ground and snorting
• Resting the chin on the cow's rump
• Bellowing and tongue lapping
• Protecting / guarding the females on oestrus

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that regulate the action in bulls during the process identified in QUESTION 4.2.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Genetics
• Hormonal influences
• Senses (sight, smell)
• Environmental factors
• Psychological factors / temperament
• Health status of the bull
• Experience of the bull
• The type of breed
• Social ranking of the bull / being over-worked / exhausted
• A newly introduced bull in a herd attracts greater attention
• Feeding / nutrition

subQuestions.questionText:
The schematic representation in the question paper illustrates the processes of a reproductive technique in farm animals: from 'Reproductive technique', a nucleus containing the DNA is taken from a donor and transferred into an enucleated egg cell, leading to fusion; this then leads to A (the blastocyst is implanted into the uterus of a recipient sheep) and B (embryonic stem cells are extracted from the blastocyst).
Identify the type of reproductive technique illustrated in A and B above.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Reproductive cloning (1 mark)
B - Therapeutic cloning (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the purpose of EACH type of reproductive technique in QUESTION 4.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Reproductive cloning: to produce an offspring that is genetically identical to the donor (1 mark)
B - Therapeutic cloning: to produce stem cells that can be used for health purposes / cell therapy (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO disadvantages of the reproductive technique illustrated in the representation above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• It is expensive
• Requires specific skills / expert knowledge
• Cloned animals age prematurely / have a limited capacity to survive
• There is an increased incidence of abnormalities
• Dystocia problems due to large offspring
• Genetic diversity deteriorates

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagrams in the question paper illustrate two different processes that occur in farm animals. DIAGRAM 1 shows: Primary germ cell → Primary spermatocyte → (A) → Spermatids → (B). DIAGRAM 2 shows: Primary germ cell → (C) → Secondary oocyte and a polar body → further division into polar bodies and (D).
Identify the processes represented in DIAGRAM 1 and DIAGRAM 2 above.
subQuestions.memoText:
DIAGRAM 1 - Spermatogenesis (1 mark)
DIAGRAM 2 - Oogenesis / ovigenesis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Label A, B and C in the diagrams above.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Secondary spermatocyte (1 mark)
B - Sperm cells / spermatozoa (1 mark)
C - Primary oocyte (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the type of cell division that resulted in C (the primary oocyte).
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Mitosis (1 mark)
(The primary germ cell divides by mitosis, during the multiplication phase, to form oogonia and then the primary oocyte.)

subQuestions.questionText:
It is important for the farmer to observe the cow prior, during and after parturition because this process can be negatively affected by many factors.
Give the term that refers to birth difficulty in cows.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Dystocia (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO problems associated with the foetus that may interfere with the normal parturition process.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• High birth weight / a large foetus / hydrops foetus
• Incorrect presentation (e.g. posterior / breech)
• Flexion of the elbow
• Deviation of the head
• Retention of one or both legs
• Hydrocephalus
• Deformities / congenital defects
• Multiple births / twinning
• A dead foetus

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that may cause retention of the placenta.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (1 mark each):
• Deficiency of vitamin A
• Infection / abortion
• Mineral deficiency / lack of selenium, magnesium or calcium
• Premature birth
• Hereditary defects / breed type
• Inertia of the uterus (weak contractions to expel the placenta)
• Over-conditioning of dry cows
• Metabolic disorders / milk fever
• Malnutrition
• Old age
• Prolonged labour
• Vaginal prolapse
• Diseases
• Induced calving
• Multiple births / twinning / abnormal births

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents the udder of a cow, with labels pointing to A (a cluster of small sacs high in the udder), a Lobe, B (a large cavity above the teat), the Teat cavity and the Teat opening.
Identify parts A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Alveoli / lobule (1 mark)
B - Gland cistern / gland cavity (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the LETTER that represents the part where milk is produced.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: A (the alveoli) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the hormone responsible for EACH of the following functions:
(a) Synthesis of milk
(b) Milk let down process
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Synthesis of milk - Prolactin / luteotropic hormone (LTH) (1 mark)
(b) Milk let-down process - Oxytocin (1 mark)
